50.0.0.en: Babylon: it is first mentioned in (Gen 10:10), where it was founded by a rebellious person called Nimrod. In it appeared man’s pride and his refusal to submit to God in the attempt to build a tower, so God confused the tongues of those gathered (Gen 11:9). It appeared as a kingdom in the eighteenth century before Christ in the reign of Hammurabi, who laid down the laws known by his name, and in the third century before Christ its greatest power appeared in the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, who seized all the surrounding countries as far as the Mediterranean Sea and triumphed over many kings, establishing his empire.

50.0.1.en: The Chaldeans: they dwelt in Mesopotamia in the tenth century before Christ, and from them Abraham came out. In this chapter and the next, God speaks in prophecies through Jeremiah against Babylon, and He gave it much speech, equal to all of Jeremiah’s prophecies about the various countries of the world, because Babylon’s evil was greater than that of the other countries. God used it to chasten His people and to chasten the countries of the world, but in the end He must chasten it.

50.1.0.en: Set up a standard: declare clearly before all, like a standard raised before everyone. Bel: an Akkadian name meaning “the lord”, corresponding in Hebrew to the god Baal; it is also one of the names of the god Merodach, and he was depicted in the form of a great head with a crown on his head and with seven bull’s horns.

50.1.1.en: Merodach: he was a god of the city of Babylon, and because of its greatness he was considered the king of the gods, and many kings of Babylon were named after him.

50.1.2.en: God declares His decision for the fall of Babylon and its shattering, despite its exalting itself over all the countries of the world, and declares the weakness of its pagan gods, the most important of which is Merodach, who is also called Bel. Because this decision must be carried out, God commands that it be proclaimed among all the peoples and not concealed from anyone, because Babylon was proud and humbled the whole world.

50.2.0.en: The reason for the fall of Babylon is the attack of the new empire formed by the union of the two kingdoms of Media and Persia, which dwell to its east and north. They will attack Babylon from the north and ruin it, so that no life remains in it and neither man nor beast can dwell in it, but it becomes deserted.

50.2.1.en: Nothing of the powers of the world that you rely on will profit you before the divine wrath. Neither its idols, nor its greatness, nor its wealth profited Babylon. So trust in God and humble yourself before Him, and you will find your protection.

50.2.2.en: [2] The return of Israel from captivity (vv. 4-8:)

50.2.3.en: 4- In those days, and in that time, saith the LORD, the children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together, going and weeping: they shall go, and seek the LORD their God. 5- They shall ask the way to Zion with their faces thitherward, saying, Come, and let us join ourselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant that shall not be forgotten. 6- My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their restingplace. 7- All that found them have devoured them: and their adversaries said, We offend not, because they have sinned against the LORD, the habitation of justice, even the LORD, the hope of their fathers. 8- Remove out of the midst of Babylon, and go forth out of the land of the Chaldeans, and be as the he goats before the flocks.

50.3.0.en: God gives good news to His people of its two kingdoms, Israel and Judah, that they will return from captivity through their repentance, their return to God and their weeping over their sins, so that God has compassion on them and brings them back to their land.

50.4.0.en: Zion: an ancient name of a fortress beside Jerusalem, and what is meant by Zion is all Jerusalem. The people of God return to Jerusalem to build the temple, pray, offer sacrifices, remember their covenants with God, and offer repentance and an everlasting covenant to live with Him.

50.5.0.en: Restingplace: the place in which the sheep rest and sleep (that is, the fold), and what is meant is the house of God and His city Jerusalem, where they worship God.

50.5.1.en: God gives the reason for His people’s straying and distance from Him: it is the lack of care of their shepherds for them; rather, because of their corruption they made the people stray far from Him. He expresses this by the mountains and the hills, where they worshiped strange gods upon them and abandoned the worship of God.

50.6.0.en: Because of the evils of the people of God and their distance from Him, they became prey to the nations, who led them astray and took them captive, whether Assyria, and before it Egypt, and after it Babylon. These enemies of the people of God were instruments of chastening in the hand of God for His people, because they strayed from Him although He is the cause of their righteousness, and they dwell in His house and His city, and He is their hope in all their troubles. But sadly they left Him and became booty for their enemies, each of whom devours them and exploits them.

50.7.1.en: God calls His people to go out of Babylon after it was struck and Cyrus, the first of the kings of Media and Persia, took the kingdom and permitted them to return to their land. God urges them to go out of Babylon and return to their land. The return of the people of God to Jerusalem and their worship of Him symbolizes the return to God at faith in Christ in the fullness of time. God asks His people to be an example to the rest of the peoples in faith in Christ, like the he goats that go out quickly from the folds and run to the pasture, and the rest of the sheep follow them.

50.7.2.en: The love of God, His tenderness and His mercy are great toward everyone who repents and returns to Him. So do not delay repentance, however great your sins or the straying you have reached; He still loves you and awaits your repentance to give you salvation and to compensate you for the misery of sin that you suffered from your distance from Him.

50.7.4.en: 9- For, lo, I will raise and cause to come up against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the north country: and they shall set themselves in array against her; from thence she shall be taken: their arrows shall be as of a mighty expert man; none shall return in vain. 10- And Chaldea shall be a spoil: all that spoil her shall be satisfied, saith the LORD. 11- Because ye were glad, because ye rejoiced, O ye destroyers of mine heritage, because ye are grown fat as the heifer at grass, and bellow as bulls; 12- Your mother shall be sore confounded; she that bare you shall be ashamed: behold, the hindermost of the nations shall be a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert. 31- Because of the wrath of the LORD it shall not be inhabited, but it shall be wholly desolate: every one that goeth by Babylon shall be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues. 14- Put yourselves in array against Babylon round about: all ye that bend the bow, shoot at her, spare no arrows: for she hath sinned against the LORD. 15- Shout against her round about: she hath given her hand: her foundations are fallen, her walls are thrown down: for it is the vengeance of the LORD: take vengeance upon her; as she hath done, do unto her. 16- Cut off the sower from Babylon, and him that handleth the sickle in the time of harvest: for fear of the oppressing sword they shall turn every one to his people, and they shall flee every one to his own land.

50.8.0.en: God declares that He is the One responsible for the chastening and ruin of Babylon, so He raises up against it Media and Persia, whom He likens to a sleeper whom God has awakened. That is, God is the Ruler of all, and He chastens Babylon because it wronged and exploited all the peoples of the earth, so He raises up peoples against it to ruin it.

50.8.1.en: These peoples come from the north, for Media and Persia attacked Babylon from the north. They set themselves in array against it, that is, besieged it. He describes Media and Persia as the mighty man who destroys what is before him and shoots his arrows at his prey, Babylon, so that it falls, and this mighty man does not return until he has achieved his aim, which is the seizure of Babylon. Babylon submitted easily at the beginning of the rule of Media and Persia, but it rebelled again, so they struck it.

50.9.0.en: The Chaldeans: they are the original inhabitants of Mesopotamia and Babylon.

50.9.1.en: Media and Persia seize the land of Babylon and take its many spoils, so that Media and Persia are greatly satisfied. Grass (pasture): herbs, and what is meant is the wheat and barley when they are threshed to separate their grain from the chaff.

50.10.0.en: Heifer: a young cow. God declares the reason for the chastening of Babylon: it gloated over the people of God when it seized its lands and spoils, like a heifer that pulls the threshing sledge to thresh wheat and barley and leaps for joy; that is, Babylon rejoiced in the humiliation of the people of God. He also likens Babylon to a horse that leaps and gives strong sounds, which is neighing, and rejoices; that is, Babylon rejoiced in the destruction of Judah and Israel.

50.11.0.en: Babylon claimed to be a mother of the peoples and was not so, because it did not have compassion on the peoples of the world but humbled them. So God speaks to these peoples and tells them that your mother Babylon, that is, the one who claimed to be your mother, has fallen into shame and disgrace because it was struck and became a wilderness and a deserted place with no water or life, although it was a fertile land; its springs dried up and it became ruin.

50.12.0.en: The LORD’s wrath was upon Babylon, so it became deserted, and everyone who passes by it is astonished and hisses, so great is his astonishment at the ruin of Babylon, which was very great.

50.13.0.en: God calls the soldiers of Media and Persia to shoot many arrows at it and kill those in it, because they rebelled against the LORD.

50.14.0.en: God continues His speech to the soldiers of Media and Persia, that they shout the shout of victory against it on every side, because it has surrendered and given its hand, so it no longer has strength to resist the soldiers of Media and Persia, who demolished it, removed its foundations and broke its walls. They take vengeance on it because it is the command of the LORD, and by this it receives its recompense: as it did evil to all the peoples, so they do evil to it and shatter it.

50.15.0.en: Sickle: a curved knife with which they gather the stalks of wheat and barley.

50.15.1.en: Because Babylon will become deserted and lose its fertility, and there is no one to sow it or reap anything from it, and those in it flee for fear of the sword of Media and Persia that kills the inhabitants of Babylon, those who left their lands when Babylon took them captive return, leave it and go back to their lands to live in security. Though Babylon was the most secure place in the world and a realm of wealth, it became a terror to everyone who stayed in it, so they fled from it.

50.15.2.en: Whoever deceives God and has no compassion on those around him and wrongs them, God takes vengeance on him, even if after a while. So do not go on in evil or wrongdoing, and return quickly by repentance, and God will have mercy on you.

50.15.4.en: 17- Israel is a scattered sheep; the lions have driven him away: first the king of Assyria hath devoured him; and last this Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath broken his bones. 18- Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I have punished the king of Assyria. 19- And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead. 20- In those days, and in that time, saith the LORD, the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.

50.16.0.en: God likens the enemies of His people to lions, and His people to sheep. When lions attack sheep they eat them as prey and rule them. The first lion is Assyria, which took the kingdom of Israel captive; then after it came the kingdom of Babylon under the leadership of Nebuchadnezzar, which took the kingdom of Judah captive and ruled it, and Israel, harshly, because it seized all the countries that had been subject to Assyria.

50.16.1.en: Satan, our enemy, takes different forms such as Assyria or Babylon, but he is violent and wants to control us. We cannot escape from his hand unless we hold fast to God. We do not fear the lions as long as we are under God’s protection, and our God is able not only to turn the lions away from us but also to punish them and protect us with a complete protection.

50.17.0.en: Broken his bones (crushed): I will make bruises in him, that is, severe contusions, and what is meant is: I will humble him and shatter his strength.

50.17.1.en: God gives good news to His people that He will lift the dominion of Babylon from them and shatter it. As He shattered Assyria at the hand of Babylon, He will shatter Babylon at the hand of Media and Persia. He chastens His people by Assyria and Babylon, but when His people repent, He punishes Assyria and Babylon for their many evils.

50.18.0.en: Carmel and Bashan: fertile places in Lebanon lying in the portion of Ephraim, which yield many good things.

50.18.1.en: Gilead: it lies east of the river Jordan and is distinguished by fertility; in it are balsam trees whose sap is a costly medicine. Gilead lies in the portion of the two tribes of Reuben and Manasseh. At the time when God punishes Babylon, He brings His people back to dwell in their land at the beginning of the rule of the kingdom of Media and Persia, so they return to their lands overflowing with milk and honey, that is, many good things.

50.19.0.en: If the nations around the people of God thought that this people was sinful and that God was punishing it, then when He brings them back to their land full of good things, God declares that He has forgiven their sins and pardoned them because they repented and returned to Him. God rewards His repentant children with abiding, stability and peace.

50.19.2.en: 21- Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod: waste and utterly destroy after them, saith the LORD, and do according to all that I have commanded thee. 22- A sound of battle is in the land, and of great destruction. 23- How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations! 24- I have laid a snare for thee, and thou art also taken, O Babylon, and thou wast not aware: thou art found, and also caught, because thou hast striven against the LORD. 25- The LORD hath opened his armoury, and hath brought forth the weapons of his indignation: for this is the work of the Lord GOD of hosts in the land of the Chaldeans. 26- Come against her from the utmost border, open her storehouses: cast her up as heaps, and destroy her utterly: let nothing of her be left. 27- Slay all her bullocks; let them go down to the slaughter: woe unto them! for their day is come, the time of their visitation. 28- The voice of them that flee and escape out of the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance of his temple. 29- Call together the archers against Babylon: all ye that bend the bow, camp against it round about; let none thereof escape: recompense her according to her work; according to all that she hath done, do unto her: for she hath been proud against the LORD, against the Holy One of Israel. 30- Therefore shall her young men fall in the streets, and all her men of war shall be cut off in that day, saith the LORD. 31- Behold, I am against thee, O thou most proud, saith the Lord GOD of hosts: for thy day is come, the time that I will visit thee. 32- And the most proud shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up: and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all round about him.

50.20.0.en: Merathaim: it lies south of Babylon, and its meaning is double rebellion.

50.20.1.en: Pekod: it lies east of Babylon, and its meaning is punishment. Utterly destroy after them: kill. God declares to the enemies of Babylon, that is, Media and Persia, who attack it to ruin it in every part of it, whether in the east or the south, that they are to punish it for its rebellion against God.

50.21.0.en: The sound of the fighting soldiers and the instruments of war will be heard in Babylon, in addition to the sounds of shattering and destruction that take place in it.

50.22.0.en: He likens Babylon to the hammer that shatters what it falls upon, for it shattered and seized all the countries of the world around it. Now God punishes it, cutting it off and shattering it at the hand of Media and Persia, and lays waste its buildings.

50.23.0.en: Snare: a trap. Taken: it fell into the trap and became unable to get out of it.

50.23.1.en: God permitted the snare for Babylon, which is the attack of Media and Persia on it, and it fell into weakness and did not know how to resist, and Babylon was ruined because it walked in evil and stood as an adversary to God by destroying His people, so it deserved to be punished.

50.24.0.en: His indignation: His wrath. God likens Himself to a great man who has storehouses from which He brought out the instruments of His wrath, and what is meant is the chastening of Babylon at the hand of Media and Persia. This is His work in the land of Babylon, in which the Chaldeans dwell.

50.25.0.en: The utmost border: the farthest east in relation to Babylon is the kingdom of Media and Persia. Her storehouses: her granaries; the granaries are the barns in which the grain is gathered after its harvest. Heaps: piles. He asks Media and Persia to attack Babylon and open its treasuries, plunder it and ruin it, so that it becomes ruined hills, and to kill all who are in it.

50.26.0.en: He required the enemies of Babylon not only to kill the people dwelling in it but also its beasts, to put an end to life in it and to all its good things.

50.27.0.en: Some of the inhabitants of Babylon fled, who had believed in God as a result of their association with the Jews who were in captivity, and came to Jerusalem, which is Zion, and declared the punishment that came upon Babylon from the God of Israel, and perhaps they declared their faith and joined the people of God.

50.28.1.en: He calls the soldiers of Media and Persia, who are distinguished in shooting arrows with the bow, to aim their arrows at Babylon and kill those in it because it wronged the people of God, Israel. Whoever assaults the people of God assaults God Himself, so God punishes it severely. This is its natural recompense, because it humbled the peoples of the earth, among whom were the people of God. As it punished the peoples, it is punished now.

50.29.0.en: On the day of the attack of the army of Media and Persia on Babylon, they kill its young men and its fighting soldiers, that is, they put an end to its strength.

50.30.0.en: The day of the attack of Media and Persia is the day of the punishment of Babylon, which wronged the peoples of the earth.

50.31.0.en: Wrongdoing Babylon falls and finds no one to raise it, because God commanded its punishment, and God permits them to burn its palaces and houses.

50.31.1.en: If you have strength and capacities, do not wrong others by them but use them to help the weak and the needy. Know that if you do not have mercy on others, God will not have mercy on you, and in proportion to how you wrong people God will judge you. [6] The punishment of the oppressor (vv. 33-46)

50.31.2.en: 33- Thus saith the LORD of hosts; The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together: and all that took them captives held them fast; they refused to let them go. 34- Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name: he shall throughly plead their cause, that he may give rest to the land, and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon. 35- A sword is upon the Chaldeans, saith the LORD, and upon the inhabitants of Babylon, and upon her princes, and upon her wise men. 36- A sword is upon the liars; and they shall dote: a sword is upon her mighty men; and they shall be dismayed. 37- A sword is upon their horses, and upon their chariots, and upon all the mingled people that are in the midst of her; and they shall become as women: a sword is upon her treasures; and they shall be robbed. 38- A drought is upon her waters; and they shall be dried up: for it is the land of graven images, and they are mad upon their idols. 39- Therefore the wild beasts of the desert with the wild beasts of the islands shall dwell there, and the owls shall dwell therein: and it shall be no more inhabited for ever; neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation. 04- As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the LORD; so shall no man abide there, neither shall any son of man dwell therein. 41- Behold, a people shall come from the north, and a great nation, and many kings shall be raised up from the coasts of the earth. 42- They shall hold the bow and the lance: they are cruel, and will not shew mercy: their voice shall roar like the sea, and they shall ride upon horses, every one put in array, like a man to the battle, against thee, O daughter of Babylon. 43- The king of Babylon hath heard the report of them, and his hands waxed feeble: anguish took hold of him, and pangs as of a woman in travail. 44- Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan unto the habitation of the strong: but I will make them suddenly run away from her: and who is a chosen man, that I may appoint over her? for who is like me? and who will appoint me the time? and who is that shepherd that will stand before me? 45- Therefore hear ye the counsel of the LORD, that he hath taken against Babylon; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out: surely he shall make their habitation desolate with them. 46- At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved, and the cry is heard among the nations.

50.32.0.en: God speaks of His poor people in the two kingdoms of Israel and Judah, and how they were subjected to the wrongdoing of Assyria and then Babylon, who led them astray and took them into captivity and did not release them but treated them with violence and cruelty.

50.33.0.en: The land: what is meant is the land of His people. God declares His responsibility for His people, for He is their Redeemer, that is, their kinsman responsible for them, and at the same time His power is great, for His name is the LORD of hosts. He will examine their case and their plea and the petitions lifted up to Him, and will do them justice, give them rest in their land and punish Babylon, which humbled them.

50.34.0.en: God declares that Media and Persia will kill the people of Babylon who dwell in it, and also the leaders of the people with the king, in addition to the king’s counselors, who are the wise men of the state.

50.35.0.en: The liars: the false prophets, the sorcerers and the astrologers. Her mighty men: the commanders of the army.

50.35.1.en: The sword of Media and Persia will kill the false prophets and the astrologers, who have great standing in the state, and also the commanders of its armies.

50.36.0.en: Their horses and chariots: its weapons of war. The mingled people: the non-Babylonian inhabitants who support Babylon, that is, its allies.

50.36.2.en: The hand of Media and Persia will stretch out to kill the horses and shatter the war chariots and destroy not only the Babylonians but their allies, and to plunder its spoils of silver, gold, cattle and every precious possession.

50.37.0.en: The enemies will dry up the river Euphrates, which enters the city from under its great wall, for they will turn the course of the river to form a great pool, so the waters of the river dry up and they storm the city from under its walls. It loses water and its inhabitants nearly die of thirst, and in all this their pagan gods, to which they clung and for which they lost their minds in following, did not rescue them.

50.37.1.en: Everything of the world’s powers and goods that you rely on is liable to pass away. So thank God for His gifts and trust in Him, and you will live reassured even if what you have is little.

50.38.0.en: Jackals: a predatory animal whose size is between the wolf and the fox.

50.38.1.en: Owls (daughters of the ostrich): the ostrich is a large bird that walks on the ground.

50.38.2.en: The enemies destroy Babylon, so people abandon it and wild beasts and wild animals dwell in it with the ostriches.

50.39.0.en: Babylon will be ruined like the ruin of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighboring countries, and all people abandon it.

50.40.0.en: God makes clear that He is the Ruler of all, who punishes Babylon for its evils, using the kingdom of Media and Persia coming from the north of Babylon, and He represents it as a sleeper whom God awakens to attack Babylon.

50.41.0.en: God shows the strength of the soldiers of Media and Persia, skilled in the use of weapons such as arrows and spears. They will besiege Babylon, standing in one rank around it, united together as one man, and so triumph over it, and at the same time treat it cruelly and ruin it.

50.42.0.en: If the king of Babylon exalted himself in his strength, now he is in great weakness before the attack of Media and Persia, and he writhes with fear like a woman near to childbirth who writhes in pain. God shows his weakness by the feebleness of his hands, which symbolize his strength, and what is meant is not only the king but all his armies, which have become weak before the enemies.

50.43.0.en: The swelling of Jordan: when the river Jordan overflows and its waters rush with force.

50.43.1.en: The armies of Media and Persia attack with force like the rush of the waters of the Jordan in its flood, and attack Babylon, full of good things, which he likens to a perpetual sea, that is, perpetual good things. But the mercy of God appears in His signal to the armies of Media and Persia, so they stop their ruin of Babylon and turn back from it. God is merciful and does not want the destruction of the inhabitants of Babylon but their repentance and abandoning of their worship of idols, and God asks to find a faithful shepherd to appoint over it to lead it to the faith. This is what happened after the Resurrection of Christ, when the good news spread through the whole world and reached Babylon. God is the strong One, able to chasten all the peoples to return to Him, and no one can stand before Him. These words were repeated in (ch. 49:19-21).

50.44.0.en: Babylon has become so weak that the least of the flock draw them out, and God lays waste their land.

50.45.0.en: The collapse of great Babylon will be heard in all the earth, and the peoples will cry out because of its fall.

50.45.1.en: Continuation of the prophecies about Babylon
